semantics: Every label the agentic-layer generator emits is listed here and scored. Gold that fails its own checksum (the invalid twins) stays scored, exactly as in the Kiji validator gold census; the per-label validity split is reported beside it and never replaces it. Layer A adjacent-address gold uses synthetic private-network host endpoints associated with a user's device. Documentation, loopback and link-local ranges are benign and scored as Layer D lookalikes instead. Layer D documents carry no gold, so every byte predicted there is a false positive. A label names a value even when it stands lines away, past a blank line, below the value, in a JSON key, sibling or nested field, or a CSV header: the labelled benign-lookalike cells of layer A are gold, and their layer D counterweights carry the same structures with no cue anywhere in the document. The address cells of layer A score every part of a whole address (house number, street, secondary unit or box, city, state, postcode) under its own label; the separators between parts are not gold, and a benign designator written beside an address (`test Suite 4`) is a recorded decoy, so covering it is a false positive. Their layer D counterweights carry the same designator words with no address anywhere. The phone-shape cells of layer A score a whole phone number, international prefix and parenthesised trunk zero included, in French dotted groups, national digit groups behind a phone label, `+CC (0)` and `00` / `001-` forms; their layer D counterweights carry dotted versions, dates and OIDs, firmware and part numbers written in the dotted phone shape, digit groups behind an order, invoice or ticket label, a signed score with a parenthesised zero, and `00`- or `001`-prefixed product, ticket, item and document codes (behind a spare country code or an unassignable NANP exchange when written in the phone's exact shape), with no phone label anywhere. The cued cells of layer A score a person's age written after `turned` (or before `geworden`), after `at the age of` (`im Alter von`), before `y/o` or before `year old female` / `year old male`, the number alone; a date of birth given one sentence after the question (`date of birth? It's ...`), the date alone; a 12- to 15-digit card number with a Maestro issuer prefix, compact or grouped 4-4-4, directly after a card label or in a card column; and a postcode in a short or foreign shape (`NNN NN`, `NN-NNN`, six digits, `NNNNN-NNN`, three digits) directly after a postal label or in a postal column. Their layer D counterweights carry the same wording and digit shapes where the text says they are not personal: the age of an object or an animal, a person turning some degrees, a date after an unrelated sentence that follows the date-of-birth question, order, tracking, transaction and timestamp numbers, and codes behind batch, seat, room, gate, error, part, invoice or build labels, some of them one clause away from a card or postal word. The URL cells of layer A score a whole URL that points at a person, scheme included: a profile page with the person's name in its path or a personal site on their surname, written with an `https` scheme or a `www` host prefix, where a structural delimiter ends it (the closing quote of a compact JSON value with sibling keys after it, JSON whose slashes are escaped as `\/`, a JSON-escaped quote, a double- or single-quoted HTML attribute, HTML element text, a Markdown link) or inside prose with an apostrophe in its path. Their layer D counterweights carry the same structures with no scheme and no `www` prefix anywhere: JSON-escaped routes and MIME types, service hosts with a path, plain and escaped, and relative links in HTML and Markdown. Layer R decoys (words spelled like or containing a name part, digit runs shared with a repeated identifier) are not gold either, so a byte predicted over one is a false positive; every repeat of a real value is gold. An unlisted label fails closed, and so does a ruling on a label the generator no longer emits. CRLF address cells score every address part and treat CRLF as one line break. Bare CR and blank-line designator twins must remain benign. German plates are whole-value gold after an immediate label; same-shape build and batch references, including near but unrelated plate words, are benign. Explicitly labelled manufacturing plate references remain benign; their whole values are false-positive counterweights even when the plate cue is immediate. Government identifier cells score only whole synthetic values directly owned by a tax, social-insurance, identity-card or national-ID cue, with natural copulas, parentheticals, line breaks and structured fields. SSN tails require an explicit ending relation. Shape-matched references, vehicle IDs, technical licences, rates and amounts remain benign even with a nearby personal-ID cue. Zero-led schemes are deliberately unassignable; Steuer-ID-shaped failures are recorded as invalid gold. ZIP/age cells score the postcode alone in shipping instructions and address suffixes, and the age alone for collective birthdays and children. Archive filenames followed by sizes, compression commands followed by counts, decimal distances or laps after turned, and explicitly stated company anniversaries are benign; their entire inserted numeric values are decoys. Generator v13 adds independently seeded class-coverage cells. Generator v13 originally put checksum-invalid coverage identifiers in layer D; v18 corrects the labelled personal national IDs. Values explicitly owned by inventory or batch references stay benign. Password field values and fake access credentials are scored gold; password-policy examples and incomplete access-key fragments are benign. Name gold covers only inserted given names and surnames; automated queues and roles are benign. German postal cells require a de-DE-first locale chain when measuring postal.de source attribution; language/region metadata alone does not change the setup policy. Generator v14 adds explicitly labelled person-linked CRM/HR identifiers in semantic JSON fields and same-line English/German cues. Public order, invoice, ticket, issue, build, commit and tracking identifiers, generic id/record_id/unique_id keys and schema-writing placeholders carry no gold. This agentic contract scores these new labels under v1/v2/v3/v4 gate use; the primary corpus contracts remain unchanged because their corpus emits none of these labels. Generator v15 adds numeric JSON scalar identifiers and repeats. Bare JSON null and boolean keywords do not supply identifier values; quoted schema labels followed by unquoted prose placeholders remain benign. Quoting a label alone does not establish an opaque string value. Generator v16 corrects the BSN benign twins: nine-digit batch, shipment and equipment references carry semantic non-person labels instead of customer-number labels. A customer number is person-linked data, so scoring it as benign contradicted the CRM/HR gold cells. No values or other cells change. Generator v17 adds independently authored field-ownership cells: grouped alphanumeric identifiers including Unicode letters and combining marks, complete ASCII-quoted scalars including literal Unicode and raw JSON Unicode escapes, adjacent personal/public assignments separated by spaces, semicolons or newlines and rejected-placeholder-then-valid-cue sequences. Each explicitly personal field owns its full scalar separately; following labels and public resource fields are never part of that value. Repeat variants use at least six digits and exact raw spellings; alphabetic-only quoted values are labelled positives without an unlabelled-repeat claim. Shape-matched public scalars and unquoted schema placeholders remain benign. Generator v18 moves the explicitly labelled checksum-invalid Aadhaar and NIR coverage cells from benign layer D to gold layer A (invalid validity). A mistyped personal national ID remains PII. CNPJ company-ID and ETH-address decoys, case/order/ticket references and customer-nested batch references remain benign. Values, UTF-8 offsets and text stay unchanged; the frozen v17 corpus reconstructs byte-for-byte. Generator v19 adds independent CRM/HR boundary cells: terminal prose punctuation excluded from identifiers, legitimate internal and quoted punctuation included, supported is/ist/lautet/whitespace next-field connectors, multiply serialized JSON with exact raw escaped gold at depths 0/1/2/3/8/9, LF/CRLF immediately after opening quotes, and tab-grouped Unicode identifiers with public-column counterweights. The literal dotted identifier AB.12.34 is measured with its sentence period excluded and its later repeat separately gold. Malformed or excessive-depth tail protection can cover public suffix bytes; those bytes stay non-gold and count as false positives. CSV/TSV headers do not create inferred person linkage. Generator v20 adds invented EN/DE/FR two- and three-part full names in lower, upper and title case across chat, tool-call argument strings, form fields and email greetings. Each given-name component and surname is separately gold, including rule-cued title seeds and uncued NER seed controls and their repeats. Whitespace is non-gold as in existing name cells. Benign service, team, customer and common-noun/surname phrases carry no gold, even behind the same cues or fields. Generator v21 adds independently seeded whole password encodings (bcrypt, PHC Argon2, scrypt/yescrypt, crypt, phpass and Django) across code and SQL surfaces, and literal password/api_token/remember_token fields. Complete stored values and repeats are gold. Incomplete or glued encodings, prices with dollar signs, unrelated public fields and password-hashing expressions are benign. SQL column positions do not infer ownership of arbitrary scalar values. Generator v22 adds PHP array literals, alternative crypt and Django salt alphabets, real spaced and pipe-containing passphrases, weak-but-real passwords, and credentials under a generic token key. Full logprob, tokenizer, schema, Laravel validation, language and masked-response contexts contain benign metadata values with no credential gold. These decoys remain false-positive counterweights even when an ambiguous password-key recognizer protects them fail-closed. The generic-token gold measures the recall cost of excluding generic code keys. Generator v21 reconstructs byte-for-byte. The v22 contexts use partition-assigned wording, syntax and value pools; rendered texts, inserted values and value-normalised templates are disjoint between dev and test. Template IDs alone do not establish the split. Generator v23 adds SQL doubled-quote and MySQL backslash-quote crypt salts at their decoded producer limits, JSON escaped-slash hash alphabets, and repeated whole-source gold. Over-limit decoded salts, truncated/overlong fixed checksums, malformed escape tails and glued suffixes stay benign. Generator v24 adds complete literal and escaped-slash hashes immediately followed by JSON separator escapes in command output, with malformed escape-tail counterweights and exact-source repeats. Generator v25 adds complete hashes after serialized line prefixes and two distinct consecutive hashes repeated twice inside one JSON stdout string. Complete JSON separator escapes before hashes are structural, while malformed escape prefixes and identifier-glued prefixes remain benign. Every earlier v24 document reconstructs byte-for-byte. Generator v26 adds the structured-input slice: labelled customer, employee and person-record IDs inside Anthropic tool_use and tool_result payloads, OpenAI tool-call arguments, Gemini function-call args, API request bodies with a person block (given name, surname and an email on a reserved domain), nested record arrays, CSV rows, NDJSON event lines and a JSON number under a labelled key. Gold is the raw document bytes of each value, including inside JSON-escaped strings; every NDJSON repeat is gold. Unlabelled numbers, amounts, timestamps, tool-call IDs and SKUs beside them are recorded decoys, so covering one is a false positive. Its layer D counterweights carry the same shapes and value shapes under public order, request and invoice keys with no person data. Every earlier v25 document reconstructs byte-for-byte.

labels.label: AGE
labels.reason: A person's age in years, the number alone, written after `turned` or before `geworden`, after `at the age of` or `im Alter von`, before `y/o`, or before `year old female` / `year old male`, in a sentence about a person. An object's or an animal's age, and a person turning some degrees, are benign.

labels.label: BSN
labels.reason: Dutch citizen service number; generated checksum-valid with a checksum-invalid twin.

labels.label: BUILDINGNUM
labels.reason: House number, or a secondary unit or box written with its designator (`Suite 312`, `Apt. 771`, `Wohnung 4`, `3. Etage`, `PO Box 417`, `Postfach 505`, the `Box` of a US military address), inside a whole synthetic address. Scored per label until a composite ADDRESS entity exists; same label as layer C. A designator and number with no address in the document is benign.

labels.label: CITY
labels.reason: Invented city name inside a whole synthetic address, and the APO, FPO or DPO post office of a US military address, which stands where a city stands.

labels.label: CPF
labels.reason: Brazilian taxpayer number; generated checksum-valid with a checksum-invalid twin.

labels.label: CREDITCARDNUMBER
labels.reason: Payment card number; generated Luhn-valid with a Luhn-invalid twin. Includes a 12- to 15-digit number with a Maestro issuer prefix directly after a card label or under a card column header, Luhn-valid and Luhn-failing in turn; the same digits after an order, tracking, transaction, reference or terminal label are benign.

labels.label: DATEOFBIRTH
labels.reason: Date of birth, with and without a cue; a date inserted as a birth date is personal data. Includes a date given as the answer one sentence after a date-of-birth question (`It's`, `It is`, `Es ist der`, `Das ist der`); a date after any other sentence that follows the question is benign.

labels.label: EMAIL
labels.reason: Personal email address derived from a synthetic name.

labels.label: GIVENNAME
labels.reason: Given name of the sender in an email header or agent payload.

labels.label: IBAN
labels.reason: Personal bank account (DE, AT, NL, FR, GB); generated mod-97-valid with an invalid twin.

labels.label: IDCARDNUM
labels.reason: Independently invented zero-led test identifiers under an explicit IDCARDNUM label; partial SSN tails require an explicit ending relation.

labels.label: IPADDRESS
labels.reason: Synthetic private-network host endpoint associated with a user's device; documentation, loopback and link-local addresses are benign.

labels.label: NATIONALID
labels.reason: Independently invented zero-led test identifiers under an explicit NATIONALID label; partial SSN tails require an explicit ending relation.

labels.label: NHSNUMBER
labels.reason: UK NHS number; generated modulus-11-valid with an invalid twin.

labels.label: SSN
labels.reason: Independently invented zero-led test identifiers under an explicit SSN label; partial SSN tails require an explicit ending relation.

labels.label: STATE
labels.reason: US state abbreviation between city and ZIP, and the AA, AE or AP code of a US military address. Kept in as in layer C; a state alone rarely identifies a person, so its place in the safety score needs an explicit ruling.

labels.label: STREET
labels.reason: Invented street name inside a whole synthetic address, and the PSC, CMR or Unit line of a US military address. Scored per label until a composite ADDRESS entity exists; same label as layer C.

labels.label: SURNAME
labels.reason: Surname, including hyphenated double surnames.

labels.label: TAXNUM
labels.reason: German Steuer-ID; generated MOD 11,10-valid with an invalid twin.

labels.label: TELEPHONENUM
labels.reason: Personal phone number (German mobile, US). Includes a reserved-range phone (NANPA 555-01xx, German 01555) written as the tail of an ORDER- style reference when a label anywhere in the same document or record names it as a phone, in any language or script; the phone is gold, the reference word is not. A 16-digit run is never phone gold: no phone number has 16 digits. Includes a whole number in a documented fictional range (ARCEP fiction blocks, BNetzA media-production numbers, Ofcom drama numbers, NANPA 555-01xx) written as French dotted groups, with a parenthesised trunk zero after the country code, or behind a `00` or `001` international prefix, the prefix included; and national digit groups with no `+` behind a phone label, synthesized non-reachable (a leading 0 that the Spanish nine-digit and Danish eight-digit plans never use). The same digit groups with no phone label are benign.

labels.label: URL
labels.reason: A URL that points at a person: a profile page with the person's name in its path or a personal site on their surname, with an explicit `https` scheme or `www` host prefix, plain or with JSON-escaped `\/` slashes. The whole URL is gold, scheme included, up to the delimiter that ends it. A route, a MIME type, a service host with a path or a relative link carries no anchor and is benign.

labels.label: ZIPCODE
labels.reason: Synthetic postal code in an adjacent address field, including intentionally unassigned CA and GB shapes. Includes a five-digit US or German postcode written inside a benign-looking structure (the tail of an ORDER- style reference, or after a currency code) when a label anywhere in the same document or record names it as a postcode. Includes the postcode of a whole synthetic address: US ZIPs in the unassigned 000xx range, German PLZ in the unassigned 00xxx range and GB postcodes in the unused ZZ area. Includes a synthesized postcode in a short or foreign shape (Swedish `NNN NN`, Polish `NN-NNN`, six digits, Brazilian `NNNNN-NNN`, three digits) directly after a postal label or under a postal column header; the same shapes after a batch, seat, room, gate, error, part, invoice or build label are benign, also when a postal word stands one clause away.

labels.label: LICENSEPLATE
labels.reason: Synthetic German registration plate, unassignable (leading-zero serial), directly after a plate label or key. The whole district, letter series and serial number are gold. Identically shaped build and batch references without an immediate plate label are benign.
